Indikator 3 measures the proportion of newly diagnosed patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] who receive a [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)]] measurement within a specific clinical timeframe—defined as 60 days before to 30 days after their first diagnosis date [^src2]. The national standard for this quality indicator is set at a target of ≥ 95% [^src1]. 

Across the reported periods, no region or healthcare cluster in [[danmark|Denmark]] has successfully met the 95% target [^src1] [^src3]. In the 2023–2024 period (July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024), the national average compliance was 76.0% [^src1]. By the 2024–2025 period (July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025), the national average improved to 83.2%, though it still fell significantly short of the overarching goal [^src3].

Looking at regional performance in the most recent 2024–2025 period, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] led the five administrative regions with a compliance rate of 87.9%, while [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] trailed at 77.9% [^src3]. In the previous 2023–2024 year, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] also led at 81.2%, and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] recorded the lowest regional performance at 72.5% [^src1].

At the healthcare cluster level, there is wide variation and notable outliers. In the 2024–2025 period, [[horsensklyngen|Horsensklyngen]] was the national leader, achieving the highest rate of 93.1%, followed closely by [[sundhedsklynge-nord|Sundhedsklynge Nord]] at 91.0% [^src3]. Conversely, [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] acts as a severe outlier and the absolute trailer, plummeting to just 41.2% [^src3]. This represents a drastic decline from the previous year, where it was already the lowest performer at 52.9% [^src1]. [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] also struggled, scoring 59.8% in 2023–2024 and improving only marginally to 73.3% in 2024–2025 [^src1] [^src3].

Trends show general improvement across most clusters from the 2023–2024 period to the 2024–2025 period. For example, [[aarhusklyngen|Aarhusklyngen]] improved from 77.8% to 88.6%, and [[sundhedsklynge-fyn|Sundhedsklynge Fyn]] rose from 81.6% to 89.8% [^src1] [^src3]. However, [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] defied this positive trend, dropping from 52.9% to 41.2%, making it a critical area of concern for healthcare quality infrastructure [^src1] [^src3].
